scope: Planning-only repair of the four SPEC-004 / CHANGE-009 quality-gate findings

findings.resolution: Child exit records an outcome but does not finalize capture. Normal completion requires close and natural EOF; a claimed interruption cannot be reclassified by later callbacks. The deadline stays active after leader exit, with a five-second interruption cleanup budget and an independent output_incomplete marker.
findings.planned_evidence: Delayed EOF, descendant-held pipes, capture errors, no unsafe signaling, bounded handle/buffer cleanup, slot release after persistence, and late-callback races.

findings.resolution: SPEC-004 owns both optional-workspace schemas and the existing single-registration default rule. CHANGE-009 references that owner. Approval uses stored concrete target ids.
findings.planned_evidence: Both tools with zero/one/multiple registrations, explicit invalid targets, cross-target ids, and registry changes between creation and approval.

findings.resolution: The 60-minute terminal window limits read availability. Startup and named lifecycle mutations prune files lazily, without a maximum disk-residence guarantee. Pending expiry retains its original time.
findings.planned_evidence: Exact availability cutoff, unchanged files during idle observational reads, each named cleanup trigger, and no running-record pruning or expiry-window extension.

findings.resolution: The existing skill/SKILL.md is explicitly included in implementation documentation synchronization, with a narrow local-approval exception, reauthorization, and terminal receipt interpretation. Shipped instructions are not changed before the capability exists.
findings.planned_evidence: Representative allowed, denied, and boundary workflow cases covering proposal, explicit local id approval, old-token denial, reauthorization, and interrupted/incomplete results.
